meta.title: QUASAR: Lowering the Loss Floor of Quantization-Aware Training with Loss-Aware Reconstruction
meta.canonical_source: arXiv v2 LaTeX source; every table below is parsed from it by tools/build_results.py
meta.source_convention: Each block carries `source` {file, label, printed}; every row/value inside a block inherits it. `printed` is the number in the v2 PDF. `bold`/`underline` list the columns typeset best/second-best.
meta.basis_warning: Table KL (Tables 1, 3, 6) comes from a separate fidelity evaluation; curve JSONs and Table 8 (ablation) use the in-loop held-out KL. They differ (Qwen INT2 Standard QAT: 0.186 in Table 1 vs 0.175 in Table 8). Never mix bases in one comparison.

healing.setting: QAD (quantization-aware distillation) on Open-PerfectBlend, 4,096 steps, asymmetric weight-only INT g128, forward-KL to the full-precision teacher

hard_tasks.caption: Reasoning, coding, and long-context results for Qwen3-4B-Thinking-2507 and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct at INT2, INT3, and INT4. We report KL and top-1 agreement between quantized checkpoints and the BF16 original, as well as benchmark accuracy.
hard_tasks.notes: bold = best, underline = second best within each bit-width block (as typeset)

standard_tasks.caption: QUASAR gives the highest fidelity in all six model–bit-width settings. Held-out forward KL, top-1 agreement, and accuracy on eight benchmarks for QAD of Qwen3-4B-Thinking-2507 and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct.
standard_tasks.notes: bold = best, underline = second best within each bit-width block (as typeset)

adaptation.caption: Comparison of QAT and PTQ methods for adapting Qwen3-4B-Base on OpenMathReasoning at INT2, INT3, and INT4. We report held-out perplexity and accuracy on five math benchmarks.
adaptation.notes: PPL = held-out perplexity; Base (no SFT) and FP-SFT rows repeat across bit blocks

checkpoint_comparison_table3.caption: Comparison of QUASAR with QAT and PTQ baselines across NVFP4, INT4, and Q4\_0 (llama.cpp GGUF format). We report fidelity to BF16 and accuracy on ten reasoning, coding, and long-horizon benchmarks.

standard_tasks.caption: QUASAR gives the best average accuracy among the quantized checkpoints. Accuracy on nine downstream benchmarks for Qwen3-8B and Qwen3.5-9B. The materialized NVFP4 checkpoints are evaluated through vLLM's native W4A4 path.

non_termination.caption: QUASAR has the lowest or tied-lowest non-termination rate among the quantized checkpoints. Percentage of generations that reach the 32,768-token output budget without stopping, using the same generations as Table \ref{tab:merged}. Lower is better.
non_termination.unit: % of generations reaching the 32,768-token output budget without stopping (lower is better)

nvfp4.curve_basis_note: The NVFP4 training curves (Figure 34) use in-loop held-out KL (e.g. Qwen3-8B final 0.0114 vs 0.0155); the 12%/15% figures are on the Table 3 basis (materialized checkpoints via vLLM). Do not compute percentages from the curves.

released_checkpoints_table11.caption: Comparison with released 4-bit checkpoints across four model families. We report fidelity to BF16 and accuracy on each model's benchmark suite. GGUF KL values are comparable only within each block. \ddagger denotes mixed NVFP4, FP8, and BF16 precision.
released_checkpoints_table11.notes: bpw includes the quantized transformer-block weights, scales, and zero-points. GGUF KL values are comparable only within each block. ‡ = mixed NVFP4, FP8, and BF16 precision.

source.data: arXiv 2608.13966v2, plot data of Figure 25 (also holds DSQ cells)

lr_sweep.setting: INT2 QAD, Qwen3-4B-Thinking-2507, 1,000 steps, global batch 32, AdamW, final held-out KL
v2_statements: Final held-out KL after 1,000 steps of INT2 QAD of Qwen3-4B-Thinking-2507 across a 50× learning-rate range.
QUASAR attains the lowest KL at every tested rate; Standard QAT diverges at high rates, while BitDistiller degrades at low rates.

summary.note: v2 plots 5 methods (30 cells) and says QUASAR is lowest at every rate. The 36-cell / 30-of-30 counts include DSQ, which is not a baseline anywhere in v2.

ablation.caption: Ablation Study: Effect of QUASAR's scale search and weighted dequantization fit on Qwen3-4B-Thinking-2507 with INT2 QAD. We report final held-out KL and its change from Standard QAT.
ablation.basis: final held-out KL from the in-loop evaluation (curve basis; matches ablation_curves.json eval_raw)

training_overhead.caption: Wall-clock time of one training step, per component and in seconds: quantization-aware distillation of Qwen3-4B-Thinking-2507 at INT3 on 8x H100 GPUs. QUASAR differs from Standard QAT only in the weight reconstruction row.
training_overhead.setting: QAD of Qwen3-4B-Thinking-2507 at INT3 on 8x H100 GPUs

memory.quote: Compared with Standard QAT, QUASAR introduces no memory overhead.
memory.why: Adam and AdamW already maintain this quantity as the second-moment estimate v_t, allowing QUASAR to reuse it without additional memory overhead.

llm_judge_int2.caption: QUASAR wins all 14 comparisons with quantized baselines. Mean per-prompt preference in [-1,1], with 95% bootstrap confidence intervals over 128 prompts. Positive values favor QUASAR. The final row compares QUASAR with the full-precision model.
llm_judge_int2.scale: mean per-prompt preference in [-1, 1]; positive favors QUASAR
